tools.name: analysis_create
tools.description: Start a new analysis run (WQA, Local SEO, Proposal, …) against a subject (client or lead). Returns the analysis record.

tools.name: analysis_get
tools.description: Get an analysis by id.

tools.name: analysis_list
tools.description: List analyses, optionally filtered by subject, type, or status.

tools.name: analysis_set_status
tools.description: Update an analysis status (pending|pulling|analyzing|review|completed|failed).

tools.name: clients_report_get
tools.description: Read a client's performance report for one channel, plus a brief on how to analyze it. Use this to diagnose performance — what is working, what is not, and WHY — then write the analysis yourself. The returned `analysis_brief` carries channel-specific rules you MUST follow; the Paid Social one constrains which levers are real for a Meta Advantage+ campaign. Serves the cached report when it is fresh, and pulls from the providers when it is stale or missing (that can take a couple of minutes). Pass refresh: true to force a fresh pull. scope: organic (default) | paid_search | paid_social.

tools.name: data_pull
tools.description: Fetch data from one provider for a subject, record the pull, and (if analysis_id is given) ingest the normalized observations. Providers: crawl, grid, http, ahrefs, semrush, gsc, ga4, localfalcon, gbp, dataforseo, windsor.

params.description: Provider-specific params. crawl: csv_content or csv_ref (an uploaded Screaming Frog export). http: urls. grid: a local rank-grid from ANY tracker (gtrack, Places Scout, a manual scan) — csv_content (headers are matched by name: keyword/search term, lat/latitude, lng/longitude, rank/position, sov/share of voice, scan date), or points: [{keyword, lat, lng, rank, share_of_voice?, scan_date?}] when you already have the rows. Optional: source ('gtrack') to label where it came from, place_id/name/address for the client report's location header, keyword and scan_date as defaults for a file that omits them. Use this instead of localfalcon when the agency doesn't use Local Falcon. NOTE: no setup is required — the grid renders in the client report with or without Google Business Profile connected — but the report serves from a cache, so tell the user to hit ↻ Refresh on it to see the import.

tools.name: data_health
tools.description: Report a subject's (client/lead) data health across every provider ever pulled for it: per-provider last attempt, last success, cache validity, and what the latest data contains (observation counts + kinds); per-kind freshness against the SLA (ranking 30d, review 60d, page/backlink/keyword 90d, …); and recent pull history. Use it to answer 'is this client's data in, fresh, and complete?' before running or trusting an analysis.

tools.name: analysis_gather
tools.description: Run every provider configured on an analysis (config.providers), reusing fresh cached pulls and retrying transient failures, ingesting all observations in one call. Returns a per-provider summary AND a coverage report (which required observation kinds are present/missing).

tools.name: analysis_coverage
tools.description: Report data coverage for an analysis: for each required observation kind (per the analysis type), whether enough is present. Use to gate checkpoints or show a data-confirmation checklist. `complete` is true only when all non-optional requirements are met.

tools.name: analysis_quality
tools.description: Run data-quality expectations for an analysis (§6c): freshness (is each kind's data within its SLA), validity (did sources return usable values, not all-nulls), and cross-source reconciliation (do overlapping providers agree within tolerance). Complements coverage — use it to surface trust signals before the strategist checkpoint. `ok` is true when there are no failures (warnings are allowed).

tools.name: observations_ingest
tools.description: Add normalized facts to an analysis. Each item is validated against its kind schema (page, keyword, ranking, backlink, review, citation, grid_point, competitor, gbp_profile).

tools.name: observations_query
tools.description: List observations for an analysis, optionally filtered by kind.

tools.name: analysis_promote_keywords
tools.description: Promote the top keyword observations from an analysis (e.g. a WQA) to its client as the tracked target keywords (max 20, ranked by search volume). This is the WQA → keyword-rankings wiring: after gathering keyword observations, call this to lock the client's tracked keywords. The analysis subject must be a client.

count.description: How many top keywords to set (default 20, max 20)

tools.name: findings_generate
tools.description: Run the analysis type's deterministic analyzers over its observations and create proposed findings (idempotent — existing findings are not duplicated). The model then reviews/tailors rather than deriving findings by hand.

tools.name: findings_create
tools.description: Create a finding (recommendation/action) on an analysis. Starts in status "proposed".

tools.name: findings_list
tools.description: List findings for an analysis, optionally filtered by status.

tools.name: findings_set_status
tools.description: Move a finding through the strategist approval lifecycle (proposed→approved/edited/deferred/rejected, with allowed reopen paths). Rejects illegal transitions.

tools.name: artifact_build
tools.description: Request generation of an artifact (workbook/report/deck) for an analysis. Returns a pending artifact; the worker renders it and fills storage_ref (download_url on artifact_get). The workbook is a read-only reference — approvals happen in the web app or via findings_set_status.

tools.name: artifact_get
tools.description: Get an artifact (status + signed storage_ref when ready).

tools.name: plan_import
tools.description: Turn an analysis’s approved findings into a scheduled 12-month engagement plan: the six-sprint frame (kickoff, technical, local, content, links, reporting) with calendar-month deliverables — technical in month 1, content batched monthly, link-production slots, and a monthly check-in cadence. Creates a new project (or extends project_id). Only approved/edited findings are included.

project_id.description: Extend this project instead of creating one

tools.name: plan_export
tools.description: Export a project plan for a PM tool. Returns CSV content (clickup | asana | monday | csv) built from the project’s sprints and deliverables; rejected items are excluded.

tools.name: integrations_set
tools.description: Store (encrypted) the credentials for a provider (e.g. ahrefs, gsc, ga4, localfalcon, gbp, dataforseo). fields is an object of secret key/values. Overwrites any existing entry. Pass verify:true to also probe the credential against the provider (free endpoint) and get a `verification` block back — worth doing, because a stored-but-rejected key otherwise fails silently weeks later.

verify.description: Also check the credential against the provider and return the result. Default false.

tools.name: integrations_verify
tools.description: Check an already-stored credential against the provider. Returns { status: ok | invalid | unknown | unsupported, detail }. `invalid` means the provider definitively rejected it; `unknown` means we could not reach the provider, NOT that the key is bad. Use this when a report or pull comes back empty before assuming there is no data.

tools.name: integrations_list
tools.description: List configured integrations — provider + which field names are set + last updated. Never returns secret values.

tools.name: integrations_delete
tools.description: Remove a provider’s stored credentials.

tools.name: leads_list
tools.description: List leads (filter by status, source, or search text).

tools.name: leads_get
tools.description: Get a lead by id.

tools.name: leads_create
tools.description: Create a lead.

expected_deal_value.description: Whole units — a fractional amount is rounded to the nearest whole number.

tools.name: leads_update
tools.description: Update lead fields.

tools.name: leads_transition
tools.description: Move a lead to a new pipeline stage (validated). Stages: awaiting_discovery, awaiting_analysis_proposal, proposal_sent_awaiting_decision, won (auto-converts to live client), stuck_nurturing, lost_followup, lost_closed, not_qualified. Legacy v1 names still accepted.

tools.name: leads_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a lead and its follow-ups, analyses, and cached pulls. Refused if the lead was converted to a client. To archive a live lead instead, transition it to stuck_nurturing or lost_closed.

tools.name: pipeline_summary
tools.description: Pipeline metrics: counts by stage + open/won value.

tools.name: followups_list
tools.description: List follow-ups (optionally by status).

tools.name: followups_create
tools.description: Create a follow-up reminder for a lead or client. assigned_to names the responsible teammate.

tools.name: followups_complete
tools.description: Mark a follow-up done.

tools.name: clients_list
tools.description: List clients.

tools.name: clients_get
tools.description: Get a client by id.

tools.name: clients_create
tools.description: Create a client. ALWAYS set `website` when the client has one — it is the key used to match their backlinks in the link workbook and their Search Console/GA4 properties, so a client created without it silently shows no link data and no organic reporting until someone adds it by hand. If you are creating clients in bulk and a website is missing from your source, ask for it rather than omitting it.

monthly_retainer.description: Whole units — a fractional amount is rounded to the nearest whole number.

tools.name: clients_update
tools.description: Update client fields.

tools.name: clients_onboarding_seed
tools.description: Create the onboarding-checklist project (invoice, onboarding email, kickoff call, platform access) for an existing client. Refused if an onboarding project already exists.

tools.name: clients_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a client and EVERYTHING attached — its projects, sprints, deliverables (with comments/attachments), content, links, follow-ups, analyses, and cached data. Irreversible; there is no undo. Prefer archiving (clients_update status: inactive) for real clients. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: projects_list
tools.description: List projects (optionally for a client).

tools.name: projects_update
tools.description: Update project fields (name, status [planning|active|paused|completed|cancelled], dates, primary_goal, kpis).

tools.name: sprints_list
tools.description: List sprints for a project.

tools.name: sprints_update
tools.description: Update sprint fields (status [pending|active|blocked|completed|skipped] — activating/completing stamps actual dates —, scheduled dates, notes, blockers, client_approved).

tools.name: deliverables_list
tools.description: List deliverables for a sprint.

tools.name: deliverables_create
tools.description: Add a deliverable (task) to a sprint.

tools.name: deliverables_update
tools.description: Update deliverable fields (status [pending|in_progress|review|completed|blocked] — completing stamps completed_at —, assigned_to, due_date, estimated/actual hours, name, description, notes, blockers, output links, depends_on [array of deliverable ids that must complete first; validated]).

tools.name: links_list
tools.description: Backlinks acquired for a client, synced from the agency's central link workbook (source URL, anchor, cost, date, status). Returns the rows plus totals (link count, spend, first/last build date). Use `links_sync` first if `synced_at` is stale.

tools.name: links_sync
tools.description: Re-read the agency's link workbook and refresh stored links. Omit client_id to sync every client (one workbook download for the whole roster). Links are matched to a client by their website domain, so a client with no website set is skipped.

tools.name: content_list
tools.description: The content calendar for a client — one row per article/page with status, topic, search volume, and draft/published URLs. The app is the source of truth for these.

tools.name: clients_set_target_keywords
tools.description: Set the tracked target keywords for a client (max 20). These appear in the client report keyword-rankings table with current rank + change. Typically set from the WQA’s top keywords. Pass keywords: string[].

tools.name: plan_templates_list
tools.description: List the reusable project-plan templates per service (onboarding, seo), each with its task list (saved override or built-in default).

tools.name: plan_template_set
tools.description: Replace the task list for one service template. tasks = array of { name, description?, deliverable_type?, executor?(claude|human), estimated_hours?, offset_days?(due = start+offset), assigned_to? }.

tools.name: plan_apply
tools.description: Apply a service template to a client as a new sprint of tasks. Give service (onboarding|seo) plus client_id (or project_id). Optional start_date (YYYY-MM-DD; due dates derive from each task's offset). Use for "add local seo", "add facebook ads plan", etc.

tools.name: team_list
tools.description: List team members (optionally by role).

tools.name: team_utilization
tools.description: Assignee × month workload rollup: task counts, done counts, estimated/actual hours, and % of each member’s monthly capacity (from weekly_hours). Includes unmatched assignee text and an Unassigned bucket.

months.description: Window length in months (default 6, from the current month)

tools.name: team_create
tools.description: Add a team member.

tools.name: team_update
tools.description: Update a team member.

tools.name: pulse_report
tools.description: The attention-first rollup: what needs a human today, grouped by client (overdue/due-soon/blocked tasks, stale or failing data pulls, analyses awaiting review, due follow-ups) and by open-pipeline lead (due follow-ups, stagnant deals, proposals in review), plus over-capacity team members. Clients/leads are ranked by urgency; quiet clients are listed as all_clear. Start here for "what should I work on".

stale_lead_days.description: Days without touch before an active-stage lead is stagnant (default 14)

tools.name: agency_get
tools.description: Get the agency profile.

tools.name: agency_update
tools.description: Update the agency profile (name, contact, branding, services, …).

tools.name: finance_pnl_get
tools.description: Get the stored Profit & Loss blob for the account (shape: { years: { [year]: { source, updatedAt, months: { [MM]: { income, cogs, opex, totals } } } } }).

tools.name: finance_pnl_set
tools.description: Replace the stored Profit & Loss blob for the account. Pass the full { years: {...} } object (transformed from the QuickBooks P&L). Overwrites the entire blob.

pnl.description: Full P&L object: { years: { [year]: { source, updatedAt, months: { [MM]: { income:{line:amt}, cogs:{line:amt}, opex:{line:amt}, totals:{income,cogs,grossProfit,opex,netIncome} } } } } }

tools.name: analysis_run
tools.description: Enqueue the durable analysis workflow for an existing analysis: gather (coverage-checked, retried) → generate findings → build artifacts. Runs async when the worker is configured; returns a job to poll with job_get plus a review_url — the strategist approves findings in the web app (or via findings_set_status) before plan_import. Does NOT auto-approve.

artifacts.description: Override artifacts to build (default per type)

tools.name: import_workspace
tools.description: Migrate an old local-first Agency OS workspace into this account. Zip the AGENCY_ROOT folder (the one containing data/ and clients/), base64-encode the zip, and pass it as zip_b64. Maps leads, clients, follow-ups, projects, sprints, deliverables, team and agency, plus WQA / local-audit / proposal analysis data; raw vendor dumps and files are preserved. Idempotent — safe to re-run (records are matched by an import marker, not duplicated). Returns a job to poll with job_get; the job result is the import summary (per-entity counts + warnings).

tools.name: job_get
tools.description: Get a workflow job (status/result/error).

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List workflow jobs, optionally filtered by ref_id (analysis/artifact) or status.

tools.name: data_catalog
tools.description: Schema catalog of every table query_run can read: columns, types, keys, relationships, enum vocabularies, and the jsonb payload shapes of observations.data by kind. Call this before writing SQL. Optionally pass `table` for one table.

tools.name: query_run
tools.description: Run one read-only Postgres SELECT over this account's data — joins, CTEs, aggregates, window functions, and jsonb operators are all fine. Tenant scoping is automatic (never filter on account_id). Single statement only, default 500-row cap (max_rows up to 1000), ~5s timeout. Use data_catalog first to see what's queryable.

tools.name: google_drive_export
tools.description: Export a built artifact to the connected Google Drive. `as: file` saves the PDF/xlsx as-is; `as: google_sheet` converts an xlsx/csv workbook into a native Google Sheet; `as: google_doc` converts an html report into a native Google Doc. Requires the Google account to be connected (Settings → Integrations → Connect Google).

folder_id.description: Destination Drive folder id (optional; defaults to My Drive root)

tools.name: clients_drive_setup
tools.description: Create (or reuse) the client’s Google Drive folder tree — a root folder named after the client, plus Content and Link Tracker subfolders — and save the folder ids on the client. Idempotent. Requires the Google account to be connected (Settings → Integrations → Connect Google).

client_id.description: Client id to set up Drive folders for

tools.name: content_push_to_sheet
tools.description: Push the client’s content workbook (content_pieces) to a native Google Sheet in their Drive Content folder. One-way: creates the sheet on first push, replaces the same sheet’s content on later pushes (stable URL). Auto-creates the Drive folder tree if needed. Requires Google connected.

client_id.description: Client id whose content to push

tools.name: artifact_publish_to_drive
tools.description: Publish a finished artifact (report/deck/workbook) into the CLIENT-VISIBLE Google Drive Deliverables folder. Explicit, human-confirmed action — the client can see this folder, so only publish reviewed docs. Requires the Google account connected.

artifact_id.description: Artifact id (must be built/ready) to publish

tools.name: support_ticket
tools.description: File a support ticket with the Agency OS team. Use this when the user hits a bug, an unexpected error, or is blocked by something you cannot fix — after telling them you're filing it. Put what they were trying to do, what happened instead, and the exact error text in `body`. The ticket automatically carries their workspace, account, recent errors and a trace id, so do NOT ask them for those or include account ids in the body.

subject.description: One line naming the problem, as a human would say it.

body.description: What the user was doing, what happened, and the exact error. Include reproduction steps if known.

severity.description: 'high' only when the user is blocked from working entirely.

tools.name: pm_boards_list
tools.description: List the boards/projects in a connected project-management tool (asana | clickup) that this workspace's stored credentials can see. Returns each board with its id, name, workspace, team and last-modified date — the input to pm_import. Read-only. Connect the tool first with integrations_set (provider one of asana | clickup, fields {pat}). A board is an Asana project or a ClickUp List; each provider stores its own credential, so both can be connected at once.

workspace_id.description: Limit to one workspace/space. Default: every workspace the token can see.

tools.name: pm_tasks_preview
tools.description: Read one board WITHOUT writing anything: its tasks normalized the way pm_import would store them (name, notes, column/section, status, due date, assignee, tags, subtasks), plus `columns` — every section with its task count and the status it will import as. Comments and files are NOT read here unless you pass include_comments:true (two requests per task) — pm_import brings them across either way. Check that mapping before importing: a column whose name is the agency’s own vocabulary ("Links", "With Creative Badges") means nothing to the word rules and lands as pending, and an archive column like "Repository" lands as pending too, i.e. as open work. Anything wrong here is fixed with pm_import’s per-board `status_map`, not by renaming the column in Asana. Also spot which assignees are missing from the team roster before importing.

include_subtasks.description: Read one level of subtasks. Default true.

include_comments.description: Also read each task’s and subtask’s comment thread and files (returned on the tasks, counted in `threads`). Default FALSE here — two extra requests each, and a preview does not need it. pm_import brings them across regardless.

tools.name: pm_import
tools.description: Import tasks from one or more boards into this workspace. Each entry in `boards` maps a board to the CLIENT whose work it is: { board_id, client_id, project_name?, project_id?, group_by? }. A board becomes a project under that client, each column/section becomes a sprint, each task becomes a task in that sprint (status inferred from the column, assignee matched against the team roster, subtasks carried across, the comment thread and its files brought across — on subtasks too — with a link back to the original). When a column’s name is the agency’s own vocabulary the word rules can only fall back to pending — pass `status_map` on that board to say where it really belongs, rather than leaving a column of finished work in the queue. Idempotent: re-running matches on the provider id and updates instead of duplicating, so this doubles as a refresh — which also means the PM tool wins on any field edited in both places (pass update_existing:false to leave existing tasks untouched). Pass dry_run:true first to see the counts without writing. Runs as a background job; poll job_get.

boards.description: Board → client mappings. Max 20 per run.

client_id.description: Existing client id (clients_list) this board’s work belongs to.

project_id.description: Import into this existing project instead of creating one.

project_name.description: Name for the created project. Default: the board’s name.

project_type.description: Project type for a created project (default "custom").

group_by.description: "column" (default) = one sprint per section; "single" = one sprint for the whole board.

status_map.description: Per-column status overrides: { "<section name as Asana spells it>": "pending" | "in_progress" | "review" | "completed" | "blocked" }. Use it for columns pm_tasks_preview shows landing somewhere wrong — matching is case- and whitespace-insensitive.

include_completed.description: Bring done tasks across too. Default false.

include_subtasks.description: Read one level of subtasks. Default true.

include_comments.description: Bring each task’s and subtask’s comment thread and files across. Default true; budget of 600 tasks+subtasks per board, top-level tasks first.

update_existing.description: Re-runs overwrite previously imported tasks. Default true.

dry_run.description: Report what would happen and write nothing. Returns the summary directly (no job).
